title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media

items.title: Uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion data
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and the unit cell $Y=(0,1)^d$ with Lebesgue measure $|Y|=1$. Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ conventions of [[def-countable-choice]]. A **uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion coefficient** is a measurable real function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ such that $a(y+k)=a(y)$ for almost every $y$ and every $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and there are constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ with $\lambda\le a(y)\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere on $Y$. Coefficients are identified when they agree almost everywhere.

For $\epsilon>0$, the physical scalar coefficient is $a_\epsilon(x)=a(x/\epsilon)$ and the associated matrix is $a_\epsilon(x)I_d$. The bounded-domain branch used on this page is $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ with homogeneous zero boundary values. Its weak equation for datum $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is
$$\int_\Omega a(x/\epsilon)\nabla u_\epsilon\cdot\nabla v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx\qquad(v\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)).$$
No coefficient regularity beyond measurability and the displayed bounds is part of this definition.

For every $\epsilon>0$, the map $x\mapsto x/\epsilon$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^d$. By [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], its pullback preserves Lebesgue measurability and takes null-set changes to null-set changes (apply the theorem also to the inverse map). Thus $a_\epsilon$ is a well-defined almost-everywhere class independent of the representative of $a$. The same result applies to every affine translation and positive dilation used in periodic sampling below, so almost-everywhere coefficient bounds are preserved under those pullbacks.

The ellipticity bounds hold almost everywhere on all of $\mathbb R^d$, not just on $Y$: periodicity transfers the exceptional null set from $Y$ to each lattice translate, translations preserve null sets by the same change-of-variables theorem, and the countably many translates cover $\mathbb R^d$ up to their null boundaries.
items.strategy: State the coefficient, cell, period, energy form, and weak boundary-value branch.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 1–3: periodic scalar conductivity, unit cell, ellipticity and zero-Dirichlet model.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems

items.title: Zero-mean periodic Sobolev cell space
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $Y=(0,1)^d$, and Countable Choice for the Sobolev conventions of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $C^\infty_\#(Y)$ be the restrictions to $Y$ of smooth $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic real functions on $\mathbb R^d$. Define
$$H^1_\#(Y):=\overline{C^\infty_\#(Y)}^{\,H^1(Y)},\qquad V_\#:=\left\{v\in H^1_\#(Y):\int_Yv\,dy=0\right\}.$$
The integral is the normalized cell mean because $|Y|=1$. Derivatives are weak derivatives on $Y$ and the periodic condition is the closure convention in this definition; no pointwise boundary trace is being imposed. Equip $V_\#$ with the inherited $H^1$ norm.
items.strategy: Fix equivalence-class and periodic-trace conventions, mean normalization, and the Hilbert norm.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §§1.2.2–1.2.3, PDF pp. 6–8: periodic cell space, corrector mean convention and variational formulation.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1–1.2, printed pp. 3–13: periodic Sobolev corrector space and cell normalization.

items.title: Separable H1-zero space and compact L2 inclusion on a cube
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $d\ge1$. Then $H^1_0(Q;\mathbb R)$ is a separable real Hilbert space. It satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(Q)}\le\|\partial_0v\|_{L^2(Q)}\le\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(Q)}\qquad(v\in H^1_0(Q)).$$
Moreover, every sequence bounded in $H^1_0(Q)$ has a subsequence converging in $L^2(Q)$. These conclusions use Countable Choice only; no Axiom of Choice or Dependent Choice is needed in the proof below.
items.strategy: Embed in a finite product of separable L2 spaces, prove Poincare on test functions, and use periodic Fourier coefficients of zero extensions with a uniform high-frequency tail bound.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.1, printed pp. 3–8: H1-zero energy space, Poincaré control and bounded-solution compactness context.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.1, PDF pp. 11–14: uniform H1-zero bounds and the compact L2 subsequence used in homogenization.

items.title: Periodic scalar cell problem
items.statement:
For coefficient $a$, cell $Y$, and zero-mean periodic space $V_\#$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]] and [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]], and for $p\in\mathbb R^d$, the **weak periodic cell equation** asks for $\chi_p\in V_\#$ such that
$$\int_Y a(y)(p+
abla_y\chi_p(y))\cdot
abla_yv(y)\,dy=0\qquad(v\in V_\#).$$
The sign convention is $p+
abla_y\chi_p$; the zero-mean condition fixes the additive constant. This definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.
items.strategy: Specify the test space, coefficient, sign convention, and mean-zero gauge.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–8: the variational cell problem and mean-zero corrector.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: periodic corrector equations.

items.title: Mean-zero Poincare inequality on the periodic cell
items.statement:
Let $Y=(0,1)^d$ and $V_\#$ be the mean-zero periodic $H^1$ space of [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. Then every $v\in V_\#$ satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(Y)}\le\sqrt d\,\|
abla v\|_{L^2(Y)},$$
and every $v\in H^1_\#(Y)$ satisfies $\int_Y
abla v=0$. Consequently $\|
abla v\|_2$ is a complete norm on $V_\#$ equivalent to its inherited $H^1$ norm.
items.strategy: Prove the zero mean of smooth periodic derivatives on opposite faces, then prove Poincare by coordinate telescoping, Jensen, Fubini, and Cauchy-Schwarz; pass both claims to the closure.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.2.2, PDF pp. 6–7: Poincare inequality on the periodic mean-zero space.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: coercivity on periodic corrector spaces.

items.title: Periodic averaging and rescaling bounds on the unit cube
items.statement:
Let $Y=(0,1)^d$, $Q=(0,1)^d$, $g\in L^1(Y)$ be extended $\mathbb Z^d$-periodically, and $\varphi\in C_c^1(Q)$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$,
$$\int_Q\varphi(x)g(x/\epsilon)\,dx\longrightarrow\left(\int_Yg\right)\left(\int_Q\varphi\right).$$
If $g\in L^2(Y)$ and $0<\epsilon\le1$, then $\|g(\cdot/\epsilon)\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C_d\|g\|_{L^2(Y)}$. In particular, for $g\in L^2(Y)$, $g(\cdot/\epsilon)\rightharpoonup\int_Yg$ weakly in $L^2(Q)$.
items.strategy: Tile the support by epsilon-cells, compare the slow factor on each cell, bound the boundary-cell remainder, and extend the weak limit by L2 density.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.1, Lemma 1.3.2, PDF p. 15: periodic weak averaging; the local cell-tiling argument also proves the stated L1 variant.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, Proposition 1.2.2, printed pp. 12–13: weak averaging of periodic rescalings.

items.title: Two-scale weak convergence for periodic tests
items.statement:
Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, let $\epsilon_n>0$ tend to zero, and let $(u_n)$ be bounded in $L^2(Q)$. We say $u_n$ **two-scale converges weakly** to $u\in L^2(Q\times Y)$ along $(\epsilon_n)$ if for every finite sum
$$\Phi(x,y)=\sum_{r=1}^m\phi_r(x)\psi_r(y),\quad \phi_r\in C_c^\infty(Q),\quad\psi_r\in C_\#^\infty(Y),$$
one has
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_Qu_n(x)\Phi(x,x/\epsilon_n)\,dx=\int_Q\int_Yu(x,y)\Phi(x,y)\,dy\,dx.$$
Here $C_\#^\infty(Y)$ is the smooth $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic class from [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. The test definition is independent of how a finite sum is represented because both sides are linear in $\Phi$.
items.strategy: Fix the Y-periodic test convention and the limiting pairing on the product space.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: Definition 1.3.3, PDF p. 13: two-scale convergence on periodic test functions.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 14–19: periodic two-scale limits.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of periodic cell correctors
items.statement:
Assume $a,\lambda,\Lambda,Y,V_\#$ are as in [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]] and [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. For each $p\in\mathbb R^d$, the equation in [[def-periodic-cell-problem]] has a unique solution $\chi_p\in V_\#$. The map $p\mapsto\chi_p$ is linear, and
$$\|\nabla\chi_p\|_{L^2(Y)}\le(\Lambda/\lambda)|p|,\qquad \|\chi_p\|_{L^2(Y)}\le\sqrt d(\Lambda/\lambda)|p|.$$
items.strategy: Use the cell Poincare bound to make the gradient norm Hilbert-equivalent and apply Lax-Milgram.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.2.2, equation (1.9) and Lemma 1.2.1, PDF p. 7: periodic cell equation and solvability context; the local proof treats the weak right-hand side by Lax–Milgram.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, printed pp. 9–13: existence, uniqueness and bounds for periodic correctors.

items.title: Two-scale compactness for bounded L2 sequences
items.statement: Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, let $\epsilon_n\downarrow0$ (monotonicity may be dropped; only $\epsilon_n\to0$ is used), and suppose $(u_n)$ is bounded in $L^2(Q)$. Then some subsequence two-scale converges in the sense of [[def-periodic-two-scale-convergence]] to a function $u\in L^2(Q\times Y)$.
items.strategy: Use the periodic sampling norm identity, a countable dense product-test family, deterministic diagonal extraction, and Riesz representation.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.2, Theorem 1.3.4, PDF p. 15: two-scale compactness statement; the countable-test and Riesz proof is supplied locally.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 15–18: related qualitative homogenization by compensated compactness, not a proof of this two-scale compactness theorem.

items.title: Periodic correctors and effective tensor
items.statement:
The library represents $\mathbb R^d$ as functions on $d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$, with standard basis $\widetilde e_j$ for $j<d$ ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]). For the usual PDE coordinate labels $i=1,\ldots,d$, write $x_i:=x(i-1)$, set $e_i:=\widetilde e_{i-1}$, write $p_i:=p(i-1)$, and set $\partial_i:=\partial_{i-1}$ in the multi-index convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. The same shift applies to vector and tensor components, so component label $i$ means library index $i-1$. By [[lem-periodic-cell-corrector-wellposedness]], let $\chi_i:=\chi_{e_i}$ be the unique mean-zero solution of the periodic cell equation. Define $\chi_p=\sum_{i=1}^d p_i\chi_i$ and define the constant matrix $A^*$ by its columns:
$$A^*e_i:=\int_Ya(y)(e_i+
abla\chi_i(y))\,dy\qquad(1\le i\le d).$$
Equivalently, $A^*p=\int_Ya(y)(p+
abla\chi_p(y))dy$. All integrals are finite because $a\in L^\infty(Y)$ and $
abla\chi_i\in L^2(Y)$. This definition does not itself assert symmetry or ellipticity.
items.strategy: State the coordinate and flux-average conventions; well-definedness is supplied by the cited cell-solvability lemma.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.2.2, equations (1.9)–(1.13), PDF pp. 7–8: cell correctors and effective matrix from averaged flux.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.2–1.3, printed pp. 9–23: correctors and homogenized coefficient.

items.title: Two-scale structure of bounded H1-zero gradients
items.statement:
Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, $\epsilon_n	o0$, and $(u_n)$ be bounded in $H^1_0(Q)$. There are a subsequence, $u\in H^1_0(Q)$, and $u_1\in L^2(Q;V_\#)$ such that $u_nightharpoonup u$ in $H^1_0(Q)$, $u_n	o u$ in $L^2(Q)$, and
$$
abla u_n\overset{2}{ightharpoonup}
abla_xu(x)+
abla_yu_1(x,y).$$
Here vector-valued two-scale convergence means componentwise convergence as in [[def-periodic-two-scale-convergence]], and $L^2(Q;V_\#)$ denotes product-measurable functions whose $y$-slices lie in $V_\#$ almost everywhere and whose squared $H^1(Y)$ slice norms are integrable over $Q$.
items.strategy: Show the two-scale limit of u_n is y-independent, test gradients against y-divergence-free fields, and construct the unique mean-zero potential by Fourier coefficients.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.2, Theorem 1.3.6 and its proof, PDF p. 17: divergence-free tests identify the gradient plus periodic-potential decomposition.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, printed pp. 15–18: related qualitative homogenization by compensated compactness; the two-scale gradient decomposition is proved locally here.

items.title: Symmetry and uniform ellipticity of the effective tensor
items.statement:
Under the scalar periodic ellipticity hypotheses of [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]], the matrix $A^*$ of [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]] is symmetric and satisfies
$$\lambda |p|^2\le p\cdot A^*p\le\Lambda|p|^2\qquad(p\in\mathbb R^d).$$
items.strategy: Use the cell equation for the symmetric energy representation, mean-zero gradients, and the minimizing characterization.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.2.3, PDF pp. 7–9: symmetric energy formula and ellipticity of the effective matrix.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, Definition 1.2.1 and Lemmas 1.2.4–1.2.5, printed pp. 11–14: effective matrix, ellipticity and symmetry.

items.title: Periodic FE-HMM with simplicial macro and periodic P1 micro meshes
items.statement:
This procedure defines a real-arithmetic finite-dimensional FE-HMM discretization. Its output is $U_H$ unless an `ExactSolve` call returns `singular-system`, in which case that token is returned; [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves the exceptional branch is unreachable for the stated inputs. It makes no bit-complexity claim, no coefficient-oracle claim, and no claim about numerically computing its exact integral entries; those entries are the mathematical values of the displayed integrals. Fix $Q=(0,1)^2$ and coefficient $a$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]]. Use the diagonal of the square from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$ as a two-triangle initial matching macro mesh. Label that shared diagonal $0$ in both triangles and each exterior edge $1$. It is a compatible labeled mesh in the sense of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. The macro input is any finite admissible descendant triangulation $\mathcal T$ of this mesh. Its cells are closed affine triangles as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].

Choose $\epsilon>0$, a micro side length $\delta>0$, $f\in L^2(Q)$, and a finite matching triangulation $\mathcal M$ of the unit square whose opposite boundary edges and vertices match under translation by the PDE coordinate vectors $e_1,e_2$ of [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]]. The periodic micro space is
$$W_{\mathcal M}:=\{z\in V_\#:z\text{ is continuous and affine on every triangle of }\mathcal M\}.$$
Here $z$ means an $H^1_\#(Y)$ class with a continuous periodic piecewise-affine representative; the periodic closure condition identifies opposite traces. Thus $W_{\mathcal M}$ is the finite-dimensional mean-zero subspace of the periodic P1 space, as proved in [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Let $V_H$ be the conforming zero-boundary continuous piecewise-affine macro space on $\mathcal T$, using [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Its inclusion in $H^1_0(Q)$ is supplied by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]].

Identify vertices of $\mathcal M$ that match under the opposite-edge translations, and order the resulting periodic vertex classes by the lexicographically least representative of each class. Let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N$ be the continuous periodic P1 nodal functions for these classes, with $\phi_i=1$ at class $i$ and $0$ at the other classes. Set $m_i=\int_Y\phi_i\,dy$. If $N=1$, use the empty basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$; otherwise use
$$\psi_i:=\phi_i-\frac{m_i}{m_1}\phi_1\qquad(2\le i\le N)$$
as the ordered basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$. The nodal basis spans the full periodic P1 space, and these functions form a basis of its mean-zero subspace.

Use the following exact solver on the systems assembled below. Given a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb R^n$, `ExactSolve(A,b)` returns the empty vector if $n=0$. Otherwise use temporary solver labels $1,\ldots,n$, with solver coordinate $i$ corresponding to library coordinate $i-1$ of $\mathbb R^n$ ([[def-function-space]]), and form the augmented matrix $[A\mid b]$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least row index $p\ge k$ whose current entry in column $k$ is nonzero; if there is no such row, return `singular-system`. Swap the entire augmented rows $p$ and $k$. For each $i=k+1,\ldots,n$, set $r=A_{ik}/A_{kk}$, replace the entire augmented row $i$ by row $i-r\,\mathrm{row}_k$, and set its column-$k$ entry to zero. After this loop, compute in order $k=n,n-1,\ldots,1$ by
$$x_k=\frac{b_k-\sum_{j=k+1}^n A_{kj}x_j}{A_{kk}},$$
using entries of the resulting upper-triangular augmented matrix. Return the vector $x\in\mathbb R^n$ whose library coordinate $x(k-1)$ equals $x_k$. All arithmetic and zero tests are exact over $\mathbb R$; the systems assembled below are positive definite.

Order macro triangles by lexicographic order of their barycenters. For each such $K$, use its barycenter $x_K$ as the single quadrature point with positive weight $|K|$, and set
$$b_K(y):=a\!\left(\frac{x_K}{\epsilon}+\frac{\delta}{\epsilon}y\right)\quad(y\in Y).$$
The affine change-of-variables theorem [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] makes this a measurable coefficient class independent of the representative of $a$, with $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere. For each PDE coordinate vector $e_j$ of [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]], in order $j=1,2$, assemble
$$G^K_{i\ell}:=\int_Yb_K\nabla\psi_\ell\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy,\qquad r^K_{i,j}:=-\int_Yb_K e_j\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy$$
over the micro-basis indices $2\le i,\ell\le N$. If that basis is empty, set $w^h_{K,j}=0$; otherwise call `ExactSolve(G^K,r^K_{\cdot,j})`, index its returned coordinates by $2,\ldots,N$, and set $w^h_{K,j}=\sum_{\ell=2}^N x_\ell\psi_\ell$. Then set
$$A^h_Ke_j:=\int_Yb_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j}(y))\,dy.$$
If the micro call returns `singular-system`, propagate that output; [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves this branch is not reached. Otherwise identify solver index $i-1$ with micro-basis index $i$ for $2\le i\le N$ and use the returned coefficient as $x_i$ in the displayed sum. The `singular-system` branch is included to make the solver instruction total.

Order the interior vertices of $\mathcal T$ lexicographically and let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_M$ be the corresponding nodal basis of $V_H$. If $M=0$, set $U_H=0$. Otherwise assemble
$$H_{rs}:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla\varphi_s|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla\varphi_r|_K,\qquad F_r:=\int_Qf\varphi_r\,dx,$$
call `ExactSolve(H,F)`. If it returns `singular-system`, propagate that output; the well-posedness lemma proves this branch is not reached. Otherwise set $U_H:=\sum_{s=1}^M x_s\varphi_s$, with solver index $s$ identified with macro-basis index $s$. This basis system is exactly the variational system
$$B_H(U,V)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla U|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla V|_K=\int_QfV\qquad(V\in V_H).$$
The macro matrix is positive definite and its `singular-system` branch is unreachable by [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Output $U_H$. The centroid quadrature is positive and exact for constants, which is the only quadrature property used in the error theorem.
items.strategy: Specify every input, sampling domain, coupling convention, matrix formula, finite solve, and singular-system output.

references.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
references.locator: §§2–3: quadrature points, periodic cell sampling, and macro assembly conventions.

items.title: No sampling resonance for period-aligned periodic micro cells
items.statement: For any dimension $d$, phase $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, and positive integer $m$, let $b(y)=a(\theta+my)$ on $Y$. Let $w_p\in V_\#$ be the unique mean-zero minimizer of $\int_Yb(y)|p+\nabla v(y)|^2dy$ and define $A_{\theta,m}^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb(y)(p+\nabla w_p(y))dy$. Then $A_{\theta,m}^{\rm ex}=A^*$ for every $p\in\mathbb R^d$. Thus a micro side length $\delta=m\epsilon$ has zero continuum sampling/resonance error, regardless of phase; a separate finite micro-space error can remain.
items.strategy: Pull the corrector back by the integer dilation, verify its weak cell equation, and average the periodic flux over the integer number of cells.

references.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
references.locator: §§2–3: periodic micro problems and FE-HMM assembly conventions.

items.title: One-dimensional nonaligned micro sampling resonance bound
items.statement:
In one dimension, let $a$ be measurable, $1$-periodic, and satisfy $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$. For a phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and ratio $r=\delta/\epsilon\ge1$, let $w_r\in V_\#$ solve $\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')v'\,dy=0$ for every $v\in V_\#$, and define $A_r(\theta)=\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')\,dy$. Then
$$A_r(\theta)=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(\theta+ry)}\right)^{-1},\qquad A^*=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(y)}\right)^{-1},$$
and
$$|A_r(\theta)-A^*|\le\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda r}=\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda}\frac\epsilon\delta.$$
No dimension-independent bound for the unaligned case is claimed here.
items.strategy: Use the harmonic-mean cell formula, split the interval into whole periods and one remainder, then compare reciprocal averages.

references.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
references.locator: §§2–3: micro sampling domains, coupling conditions, and effective coefficient reconstruction.

items.title: Periodic scalar Dirichlet homogenization on the unit cube
items.statement:
Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, let $a$ be a measurable $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic scalar coefficient with $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$, and let $f\in L^2(Q)$. For $\epsilon>0$ let $u_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ be the unique weak solution
$$\int_Qa(x/\epsilon)\nabla u_\epsilon\cdot\nabla v=\int_Qfv\qquad(v\in H^1_0(Q)).$$
Let $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$ be the unique solution with $A^*$ from [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]] in place of $a(x/\epsilon)I$. Then as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $u_\epsilon\rightharpoonup u_0$ in $H^1_0(Q)$.
items.strategy: Obtain the two-scale gradient limit, identify the cell equation using epsilon-scaled oscillating tests, average the flux, and use uniqueness to remove subsequences.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.1, Theorem 1.3.1 and proof, PDF pp. 12–15; §1.3.2, equations (1.48)–(1.50), PDF pp. 18–19: periodic Dirichlet homogenization and its two-scale variational derivation.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.3, Theorem 1.3.2 and the following Dirichlet discussion, printed pp. 15–18: qualitative homogenization and flux identification by compensated compactness.

items.title: Antisymmetric periodic flux potential
items.statement:
For each column $j$, define the mean-zero periodic flux $q^j(y)=a(y)(e_j+\nabla\chi_j(y))-A^*e_j$. There is a mean-zero periodic tensor $\sigma^j\in H^1_\#(Y;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ such that $\sigma^j_{ik}=-\sigma^j_{ki}$ and
$$q_i^j=\sum_{k=1}^d\partial_{y_k}\sigma^j_{ik}\quad\text{in distributions on the torus},\qquad \|\sigma^j\|_{H^1(Y)}\le C_d\|q^j\|_{L^2(Y)}.$$
items.strategy: Solve a mean-zero periodic Poisson problem by Lax-Milgram; prove the vector-potential divergence vanishes by Fourier coefficients.

references.title: Zhongwei Shen, Lectures on Periodic Homogenization of Elliptic Systems
references.locator: Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 26–27: Proposition 2.1.1 constructs a mean-zero periodic antisymmetric flux potential from the mean-zero divergence-free corrector flux by solving a periodic Poisson equation.

items.title: Well-posedness of the finite FE-HMM micro solves
items.statement:
For every macro cell $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], the coefficient $b_K$ satisfies $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$. For each $p\in\mathbb R^2$, both the full cell problem on $V_\#$ and its restriction to $W_{\mathcal M}$ have unique solutions $w_{K,p}$ and $w^h_{K,p}$. The tensors
$$A_K^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w_{K,p}),\qquad A_K^hp=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w^h_{K,p})$$
are symmetric and satisfy $\lambda I\le A_K^{\rm ex},A_K^h\le\Lambda I$. Consequently the macro FE-HMM system in the algorithm has a unique solution. The exact Gaussian-elimination calls specified there terminate without the `singular-system` branch and return the unique solutions of the assembled micro and macro variational systems.
items.strategy: Restrict the uniformly elliptic form to the finite periodic subspace and apply Lax-Milgram.

items.title: Boundary-cutoff corrector estimate for regular periodic data
items.statement:
Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$ be scalar and periodic, and let $f\in L^2(Q)$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $u_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ solve the oscillatory weak equation with coefficient $a(x/\epsilon)$, and suppose $u_0\in C^2(\overline Q)\cap H^1_0(Q)$ solves the homogenized equation with the same datum $f$. For $0<\epsilon\le1/4$ choose a Lipschitz cutoff $\eta_\epsilon$ equal to zero where $\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial Q)\le\epsilon$, equal to one where that distance is at least $2\epsilon$, and with $|\nabla\eta_\epsilon|\le C_d/\epsilon$. Define
$$w_\epsilon(x)=u_0(x)+\epsilon\eta_\epsilon(x)\sum_{j=1}^d\chi_j(x/\epsilon)\partial_ju_0(x).$$
Then $w_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ and, for a constant independent of $\epsilon$,
$$\|\nabla(u_\epsilon-w_\epsilon)\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|u_\epsilon-u_0\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C\sqrt\epsilon.$$
The constant may depend on $d,\lambda,\Lambda$, the fixed corrector and flux-potential $H^1(Y)$ norms, $\|u_0\|_{C^2(\overline Q)}$, and the cutoff profile. No rate is asserted without this regularity and periodicity.
items.strategy: Construct the cutoff expansion, bound its boundary-strip residual, use the antisymmetric flux potential to gain epsilon in the interior, and test the residual equation with the error.

items.title: Energy identity for FE-HMM micro tensor error
items.statement:
For a fixed macro sample $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], let $b_K$ be its sampled coefficient, $w_{K,p}\in V_\#$ the full periodic cell solution, and $w^h_{K,p}\in W_{\mathcal M}$ its micro P1 solution from [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Set $\|
abla v\|_{b_K}^2=\int_Yb_K|
abla v|^2$. Then
$$p\cdot(A_K^h-A_K^{m ex})p=\|
abla(w^h_{K,p}-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}^2\ge0,$$
and for any $z_h\in W_{\mathcal M}$,
$$\|
abla(w^h_{K,p}-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}\le\|
abla(z_h-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}.$$
In particular $\|A_K^h-A_K^{m ex}\|_{op}\le\eta_K^2$, where $\eta_K=\sup_{|p|=1}\inf_{z_h\in W_{\mathcal M}}\|
abla(z_h-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}$ and $\|M\|_{op}=\sup_{|p|=1}|Mp|$.
items.strategy: Subtract the continuous and discrete variational equations and use the energy-minimizing characterization.

items.title: FE-HMM macro, micro, and sampling error separation
items.statement:
Let $U_H$ be the FE-HMM solution from [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]] on a matching macro triangulation of $Q=(0,1)^2$, and let $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$ solve the homogenized equation with coefficient $A^*$. For each macro cell let $A_K^{\rm ex}$ be the exact periodic-coupling sampled tensor and $A_K^h$ its discrete micro tensor. Define
$$\Delta_{\rm micro}=\max_K\|A_K^h-A_K^{\rm ex}\|_{op},\qquad \Delta_{\rm res}=\max_K\|A_K^{\rm ex}-A^*\|_{op},\qquad \Delta=\Delta_{\rm micro}+\Delta_{\rm res},$$
and $\eta_H=\inf_{V\in V_H}\|\nabla(u_0-V)\|_{L^2(Q)}$. If $\Delta<\lambda$, then
$$\|\nabla(U_H-u_0)\|_2\le\frac{\lambda+\Lambda}{\lambda-\Delta}\,\eta_H+\frac{\Delta}{\lambda-\Delta}\,\|\nabla u_0\|_2.$$
The first term is macro best approximation; the second is explicitly split by $\Delta_{\rm micro}$ and $\Delta_{\rm res}$. By [[lem-fehmm-micro-tensor-approximation-error]], $\Delta_{\rm micro}\le\max_K\eta_K^2$. If every micro ratio is an integer, [[lem-fehmm-period-aligned-sampling-has-zero-resonance]] gives $\Delta_{\rm res}=0$. The condition $\Delta<\lambda$ is a sufficient perturbation condition; no arbitrary-scale accuracy is asserted.
items.strategy: Bound the bilinear-form perturbation by the tensor discrepancy, prove coercivity, and derive a finite-dimensional energy-Strang estimate.

title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media — Examples

items.title: Layered medium: harmonic normal and arithmetic tangential means
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $0<\rho<1$, and let $a(y)=a_1$ for $0<y_1<\rho$ and $a(y)=a_2$ for $\rho<y_1<1$, extended periodically, where $a_1,a_2>0$. Then
$$A^*=\operatorname{diag}\left(\left(\frac\rho{a_1}+\frac{1-\rho}{a_2}\right)^{-1},\ \rho a_1+(1-\rho)a_2,\ldots,\rho a_1+(1-\rho)a_2\right).$$
items.strategy: Solve the one-dimensional normal flux equation and test the tangential cell equation directly.

items.title: High contrast destroys contrast-independent conditioning
items.statement:
In dimension $d\ge2$, let $a_\kappa(y_1)=\kappa$ on the first half-period and $1$ on the second, with $0<\kappa\le1$. Then
$$A^*_\kappa=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2\kappa}{1+\kappa},\frac{1+\kappa}{2},\ldots,\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\right),\qquad \operatorname{cond}_2(A^*_\kappa)=\frac{(1+\kappa)^2}{4\kappa}\longrightarrow\infty\quad(\kappa\downarrow0).$$
Thus pointwise ellipticity of each fixed coefficient does not give a contrast-independent condition number.
items.strategy: Use the exact layered tensor from the cell formulas and compute its two eigenvalues.

items.title: A nonaligned one-dimensional micro window has resonance error
items.statement: Let $a(y)=1$ on $[0,1/2)$ and $a(y)=2$ on $[1/2,1)$, extended with period one. At phase $\theta=0$ and nonaligned ratio $r=\delta/\epsilon=3/2$, the exact sampled harmonic tensor is $A_r=6/5$, whereas $A^*=4/3$. The discrepancy is $2/15>0$ even though the continuum coefficient is periodic.
items.strategy: Integrate the reciprocal coefficient over one and one-half periods and compare the two reciprocal averages.

items.title: FE-HMM energy error ledger with distinct components
items.statement:
Suppose a verified FE-HMM ledger has ellipticity bounds $\lambda=1$, $\Lambda=2$, macro best-approximation bound $\eta_H\le1/10$, micro tensor discrepancy bound $\Delta_{\rm micro}\le1/20$, sampling discrepancy bound $\Delta_{\rm res}\le1/20$, and homogenized energy norm $\|\nabla u_0\|_2\le1$. Then the macro theorem certifies
$$\|\nabla(U_H-u_0)\|_2\le\frac49.$$
These are conditional certified inputs for the ledger; the example makes no claim that they arise for every coefficient, scale ratio, or mesh.
items.strategy: Compute the discrepancy threshold, coercivity factor, and each error contribution exactly.
